reasons.reader_question: The horn interrupts the queen mid-sentence, and Rema's roll forces a concrete question: what the queen signs before a recorder.
reasons.change: The queen loses her paper leverage over the forty and admits the raids publicly. The 'living mouth' line muddies 'none left'.
reasons.romance_movement: New reason: Devan lets her grieve a man he cannot mourn, without arguing. It builds on trust rather than replaying an old refusal.
reasons.shown_chemistry: Responsive action carries it: he sits to her left, sets his palm up without reaching, waits until she turns, and jokes about Pepper.
reasons.character_logic: Neela, a rules expert, wrongly says Chathu still witnesses all forty. The discovery begins with an accidental cheek-press, which is slightly convenient.
reasons.stakes_and_cost: Haran's warning prices the exposure, but Neela's refusal to sign has no stated cost in spears, truce or Company lives.
reasons.prose: The writing is concrete and well voiced, with no banned phrases. Four or five 'silent hall' beats repeat, and the well section over-explains Devan's restraint.
reasons.continuity: Self-named members void every other witness (F008). Twenty-nine of the forty have named, so Chathu cannot cage 'any of them'. That conflicts with the bible.

fixes: At 'Chathu saw every one of them turn, and he can say it aloud to any of them', the line breaks the self-naming rule (worldbuilding collapse). Change it to: the named are free of him entirely, and only the eleven who have not chosen still answer to his mouth. Have Neela make the same correction to the queen's 'write the forty true': he can write only the eleven, and only if someone gives him resin. Update F1106 to match.

Cut repeated silence beats: 'Nobody spoke. Haran took his shoulder off', 'Nobody in the hall breathed', 'She had not known how loud a hall could be', 'It landed in the hall and nothing answered it'. Keep at most two (repetitive tension at line level). Replace the others with one specific reaction each, for example Haran's sergeants exchanging a look or Usha's hand going to her cuff.

At 'his left hand came up and settled on the back of her neck', the nape is Neela's established forced-turning trigger (F1063), and the touch passes unremarked. Either give one beat of the old stiffening that she lets go because it is his hand, or move the hand to her shoulder and save the nape for ch31. Also cut 'where Ammu's blue cloth should have been': the cloth lies at the blackbark tree (F624).
reader_question: What has Justice Rema brought on the high court's roll, and will the queen sign the charter now that a recorder is at the gate?
new_facts_assessment: F1105 (Chathu taught her letters at ten) fits F232/F360 and adds needed grief texture. F1106 breaks the self-naming rule: Chathu witnesses only the eleven unnamed, so limit it to them. F1107 (fourteen hundred) is stale after the officer losses; say 'still twelve hundred or more' or keep it vague. F1108 is consistent with F520 and Rema's crown role.
